papers.title: With Leverage, the Gambler is Not the One Who Gets Ruined
papers.abstract: In this note we explore the following simple question: How does the classic \emph{gambler's ruin} phenomenon change if we allow the gambler \emph{financial leverage}? We show that, with a moderate amount of leverage, it is possible for an (idealized) gambler to sustain seemingly improbable profits over a remarkably long time horizon without ever going bankrupt, \emph{even} if the gambler makes only fair bets. With a leverage ratio of $L = 10$ (less than what Lehman Brothers Holdings had from 1995--2008), the probability of multiplying one's money by $1000\times$ without going bankrupt is roughly $50\%$. More generally, given $L$-fold leverage, and given the goal of multiplying one's money by a factor of $r > 1$, the optimal gambling strategy has probability roughly $r^{-1/L}$ of success. The results in this note are designed as part of the course development for the CMU randomized algorithms course.

papers.title: A subquadratic upper bound for the mixing time of the Thorp shuffle
papers.abstract: Let $n=2^d$. We prove that the worst-start total-variation mixing time of the full labelled Thorp shuffle satisfies, for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1$, \[ t_{\mathrm{mix}}(\varepsilon) \le C_* d^{5/3}+O_\varepsilon\!\left(d^{4/3}\log(d+2)\right), \qquad C_*=5.1536951454\ldots . \] Time is measured in ordinary Thorp shuffles. This improves the previously published full-deck upper bound $O(d^3)$ of Morris. The geometric starting point is elementary: label the $n=2^d$ positions by binary strings. One physical Thorp shuffle is a random swap layer on one coordinate matching of the $d$-dimensional cube, followed by a deterministic cyclic rotation of the coordinates. In a rotating frame that deterministic rotation disappears, so $d$ successive physical shuffles become one \emph{sweep}: one independent random swap layer in each coordinate direction. The proof then combines five ingredients. First, a collision-graph representation and negative dependence give pointwise smoothing for ordered marked cards. Second, an entropy argument is sharpened by moving an endpoint moment up to the critical exponent $\beta_c=\log_2(3/2)$, yielding an entropy-preparation clock $s^2/(2\log(3/2))+O(s\log s)$. Third, exact multiplicities in the ordered $h$-tuple permutation representation amplify marked-card bounds into Fourier operator and energy estimates on low representation levels. Fourth, entropy truncation produces a positive mixture whose regular component retains the marked-card budget. Finally, only two long blocks need this entropy regularization: a shorter third block is used solely for additional low-level smoothing. Optimizing the three block lengths gives the constant above.

papers.title: Weight-adapted ANOVA kernels for high-dimensional periodic approximation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct normalized periodic kernels from univariate functions satisfying suitable moment conditions and derive sufficient conditions for high-order convolution approximation. Two computable quasi-interpolation schemes are obtained by discretizing the convolution integral using either a full tensor grid or random samples. In each case, the analysis separates the continuous convolution error from the error introduced by discretization. The contribution of kernel energy to the error exposes the dimensional dependence of tensor-product kernels and motivates our weight-adapted ANOVA constructions. Under suitable summability conditions on the weights, we establish convolution error and kernel energy estimates that yield dimension-uniform error bounds for the resulting quasi-interpolants. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical convergence rates and illustrate the effect of coordinate weighting on dimensional dependence.

papers.title: From Global to Tail Convergence: Dynamics of $\alpha$-Stable Score-Based Generative Models
papers.abstract: Score-based generative models driven by $\alpha$-stable L{\'e}vy processes have been proposed as an alternative to Brownian diffusion models, with empirical evidence suggesting improved sampling and better modeling of heavy-tailed data. Yet theoretical guarantees for these models remain limited. We develop a non-asymptotic convergence analysis for scale-preserving $\alpha$-stable generative dynamics, covering both compactly supported and power-law targets. In p-Wasserstein distance, we quantify the effects of early stopping, initialization, score approximation, and time discretization, and show exponential decay of the initialization error. A comparison with Brownian dynamics reveals that global Wasserstein convergence alone does not fundamentally distinguish the two models: both initialization errors decay exponentially with the forward horizon on the common class of heavy-tailed targets. A sharp separation emerges instead in the tails. At any positive generation time, stable dynamics produces power-law tails with index $\alpha$, whereas Brownian dynamics remains light-tailed. For a target with tail index $\nu$, asymptotically correct extreme-quantile scaling is possible precisely when $\alpha$=$\nu$. These results identify tail-index matching as a principled mechanism behind the ability of stable generative models to capture extreme events.

papers.title: Wong--Zakai Convergence and FNO Learning for Stochastic Volterra Equations
papers.abstract: This paper studies Wong--Zakai convergence and Fourier neural operator learning for stochastic Volterra integral equations (SVIEs) describing random systems with memory. A Wong--Zakai theorem establishes convergence of pathwise solutions driven by piecewise linear approximations of Brownian motion to the corresponding SVIE solution. This convergence provides a foundation for using mirror-padded Fourier neural operators to learn the solution operator mapping initial conditions and driving noise to entire solution trajectories. Numerical experiments demonstrate competitive prediction accuracy and generalization to temporal grids finer than those used for training, while assessing the influence of padding and computational cost. As a follow-up to \citet{LKP:26}, this study extends their operator-learning framework to SVIEs through separate convergence and approximation analyses tailored to convolutional memory.

papers.title: On the discrete Fisher information
papers.abstract: We investigate a discrete analogue of the Fisher information. By using a discrete Laplacian operator, we can construct a discrete analogue of the score function and hence of the information. This provides a natural framework for establishing several information-theoretic inequalities in the discrete setting.

papers.title: Entropic Inequalities and Limit Theorems in Boolean Probability
papers.abstract: We study Boolean entropy and Fisher information in information inequalities and the Boolean central limit theorem. We prove a fractional Stam inequality for the Boolean Fisher information associated with arbitrary fractional partitions of subset sums, and derive an entropy power inequality for sums of Boolean independent random variables and its weighted version. We then establish a Boolean analogue of Barron's entropy convergence result along the Boolean central limit theorem: Boolean entropy converges to the entropy of the Rademacher law if and only if the initial entropy is finite. Furthermore, under a finite fourth moment, in the Boolean central limit theorem, we obtain \[ \Gamma(\mu_n\mid\mathbf b)= \frac{m_4(\mu)-1-m_3(\mu)^2}{2}\frac{\log n}{n} +o\!\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right), \] with an explicit example showing sharpness. For symmetric laws with finite fourth moment and finite Boolean Fisher information, \[ \Psi(\mu_n\mid\mathbf b) =2\bigl(m_4(\mu)-1\bigr)\frac{\log n}{n} +o\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right). \] Our approach is based on the Nevanlinna representation of Cauchy transforms.

papers.title: Rare Event Simulation of Quantum Error-Correcting Circuits
papers.abstract: We describe a practical approach for accessing the logical failure rates of quantum error-correcting (QEC) circuits under low physical (component) failure rate regimes. Standard Monte Carlo is often the de facto approach for studying the failure rates of quantum circuits. However, in the study of fault-tolerant error-correcting circuits, the ability to extend this approach to low physical failure rates is limited. In particular, the use of Monte Carlo to access circuits that are relatively large or have high correcting power becomes more difficult as we lower the input failure rates of the individual components (gates) in the circuit. For these reasons, many simulations studying the circuit model go no lower than end-to-end logical failure rates in the 10^{-6} regime. In this report, we outline an approach that borrows from earlier work by Bravyi and Vargo to the more complex circuit noise model. Earlier works studied both the capacity and phenomenological noise models, but the work is insufficient for generating similar simulations in the circuit-noise model. To the best of our knowledge, our team is the first to develop a full prescription of the rare event simulation by splitting technique for the circuit-based noise model. We have also generated promising results that are confirmed by standard Monte Carlo simulation under an accessible regime. This work shows that we can access noise in the circuit-model prescription of quantum error-correcting code to failure rates below 10^{-20} regime.

papers.title: Minimax Binary Counting under Shuffle Privacy: Poisson Limits and Randomized-Response Optimality
papers.abstract: We study estimation of a deterministic binary count from the shuffled outputs of a common single-message local channel. Privacy is required for every neighboring composition at fixed global parameters $(\varepsilon,\delta)$, and estimators may be biased. We obtain uniform critical Poisson and Skellam approximations and characterize the limiting minimax risk as an infimum over finite observed-mark Poisson experiments. Let $\Lambda$ be the noise intensity required by the boundary Poisson-shift profile and let $\lambda_{\min}$ be the intensity required by the full composition-maximized randomized-response profile. Binary randomized response is asymptotically minimax optimal if and only if $\Lambda=\lambda_{\min}$. When $\Lambda<\lambda_{\min}$, the minimax value lies strictly between $(\Lambda+\lambda_{\min})/2$ and $\lambda_{\min}$, and a randomized-response construction with observed rare marks strictly improves on binary randomized response. We give a finite-sample certified example. Binary randomized response is strictly suboptimal at $\varepsilon=0$ for every $0<\delta<1$, and this persists for sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$ at each fixed target. For every fixed positive $\varepsilon$, strict suboptimality also occurs along a sequence of fixed privacy targets tending to zero. The variational characterization permits approximation by finite marked channels; it does not assert that a finite optimizer exists.

papers.title: Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with an RBF Kernel
papers.abstract: Gaussian processes (GPs) are widely used across machine learning, spatial statistics, time-series analysis, optimization, Bayesian statistics, and scientific applications. A central component of a GP model is its kernel, which is typically specified through a parametric family. Among the most widely used choices is the radial basis function (RBF), also known as the squared exponential or Gaussian kernel, owing to its simple form, smoothness, and flexibility. In practice, the kernel parameters are routinely estimated by the maximum likelihood estimators (MLEs), as implemented by standard GP software. Despite this widespread use, the asymptotic behavior of the MLEs remains poorly understood under fixed-domain asymptotics, even for the RBF kernel. The main difficulty arises from the increasingly strong dependence among densely sampled observations and the nonlinear dependence of the covariance matrix on the kernel parameters. In this paper, we address this gap by providing, to the best of our knowledge, the first complete asymptotic characterization of the joint MLE of the spatial variance, lengthscale, and nugget variance under fixed-domain asymptotics. We establish consistency, derive convergence rates for all three parameters, prove joint asymptotic normality, and show that these rates are minimax optimal.

papers.title: Interior smoothness and zero-variance geometry for finite-maturity Heston American puts
papers.abstract: We study finite-maturity American puts in the Heston model without the Feller condition. At positive variance, the exercise boundary is smooth and strictly decreasing in remaining maturity and variance. At zero variance, the endpoint is locally Lipschitz in remaining maturity, the boundary moves with bounded speed in maturity uniformly down to zero variance, and it extends continuously to the axis. Each boundary slice at positive maturity has a regular $C^1$ closure tangent to the zero-variance axis, its stock threshold has variance derivative tending to minus infinity, and both partial derivatives of the inverse boundary graph vanish along the slice. The continuation premium at the axis contact stock is of order variance, and as a consequence smooth fit fails in the variance direction at the axis. At expiry the whole boundary, including its axis edge, converges to the strike. We give quantitative boundary gap bounds, an exact limiting weighted boundary Hessian, and vertical identities retaining the maturity term. Exact boundary gap equivalents remain open.

papers.title: KPP type reaction--diffusion equations in narrow tubes with degenerating boundary and generalized second order operators
papers.abstract: We consider a reaction--diffusion equation with Kolmogorov--Petrovskii--Piskunov (KPP) nonlinearity and Neumann boundary conditions in a narrow tube $G^{\varepsilon,\delta}\subset\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{n}$ of width of order $\varepsilon$. The tube is chosen from a family indexed by a second parameter $\delta>0$, whose boundary $\partial G^{\delta}$ is smooth for each $\delta>0$ but degenerates as $\delta\downarrow0$. In the iterated limit $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ followed by $\delta\downarrow0$ the problem becomes a Cauchy problem on the line whose spatial operator is a generalized second order differential operator $D_{v}D_{u}$ in the sense of Feller, rather than a classical second order elliptic operator. Solutions of the limiting problem need not be differentiable in $x$, so they must be understood in a generalized sense. Using the Feynman--Kac representation, we prove that the limiting problem has a unique generalized solution. When the cross sectional volume is bounded above and below, we also prove that this solution is H\"older continuous in $t$ with exponent $1/2$, locally uniformly in $x$, whenever it is Lipschitz continuous in $x$. Under the same volume bounds, this Lipschitz condition holds when the initial function and the nonlinearity are Lipschitz continuous in $x$. Finally we prove that the solutions in the narrow tubes converge to the generalized solution uniformly on compact time intervals in the same iterated limit if the tube, the initial function, and the nonlinearity are periodic in $x$.

papers.title: Packing intermediate dimensions of measures and applications
papers.abstract: We introduce a spectrum of dimensions of measures, the \emph{packing intermediate dimensions} $\dim_{P,\theta}\mu$, $\theta\in(0,1]$, of a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and the \emph{quasi-Hausdorff dimension} $\dim_{qH}\mu$. We show that this spectrum encodes the information on $\mu$ that governs the packing dimension of its projections and H\"{o}lder images. First, $\dim_{qH}\mu$ is the exact threshold for the packing dimension profiles of Falconer and Howroyd: for every real $0<s\leq n$, $\dim_P^s\mu=s$ if and only if $s\leq\dim_{qH}\mu$. Second, we prove a lower bound for the profiles in terms of $\dim_H\mu$, $\dim_{P,\theta}\mu$ and the Assouad dimension of $\operatorname{supp}\mu$, which improves the bound of Falconer and Mattila, the best previously known general lower bound for the packing dimension of projected measures. The improvement is strict whenever $\dim_H\mu<\dim_P\mu$ and $\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}\mu)<n$, and when $\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}\mu)=n$ it occurs exactly when $\dim_{P,\theta}\mu$ exceeds an explicit universal lower bound for some $\theta$ in an explicit range. We present examples of measures with $\dim_H\mu<\dim_P\mu<\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}\mu)=n$ for which our bound gives the exact value $\dim_P\mu_V=\min\{\dim_P\mu,m\}$ for almost every $m$-dimensional subspace $V$, whereas the bound of Falconer and Mattila is strictly smaller. As applications, for a large family of random $\alpha$-H\"{o}lder maps $f_\omega:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$, we prove that, for compactly supported $\mu$, $\dim_P\mu_{f_\omega}=m$ almost surely if and only if $\alpha m\leq\dim_{qH}\mu$, and that the packing analogue of Kahane's formula holds for fractional Brownian motions if and only if $\dim_{qH}\mu=\dim_P\mu$. Analogous results are obtained for analytic sets.

papers.title: $L^p_\mu$-Normed Spaces of Bounded Multilinear Operator
papers.abstract: We study the spaces of bounded multilinear operators $\mathcal L^i(X,Y)$ endowed with $L^p_\mu$-norms, where $X,Y$ are normed spaces and $\mu$ is a measure with $p$-moments. These are norms without taking a quotient, under suitable support conditions. The topology induced coincides with the strong operator and compact-open topologies on operator-norm-bounded subsets. Furthermore, we identify the completion of these spaces with spaces of Hilbert--Schmidt operators on the reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) for $p=2$; with iterated $\gamma$-radonifying multilinear operators on the RKHS in the Gaussian case, for general $p$.

papers.title: Gaussian rigidity and width of measures
papers.abstract: Given $0\le m<n$ and a positive Radon measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^n$ with at most polynomial growth, assume that it has finite $m$-dimensional \emph{Gaussian discrepancy}, defined as $$\mathcal D(\mu):=\limsup_{R\to\infty}\Bigl[R^2\sup_{x\in\mathrm{spt}\mu}|G_R^\mu(x)-1|\Bigr],$$ where $G_R^\mu(x):=(4\pi R^2)^{-m/2}\int_{\mathbb R^n} e^{-|z-x|^2/(4R^2)}\,d\mu(z)$. Provided that $\mu$ admits a flat blow-down $\mathcal H^m\llcorner V$ (an assumption that cannot be dropped entirely), we prove that there exists a finite (smallest) $0\le\delta<\infty$, called the \emph{width} of $\mu$, such that $$\mathrm{spt}\mu\subseteq \bar B_\delta(V+x_0),\quad \delta^2\le C(m,n)\mathcal{D}(\mu),$$ where $\bar B_\delta(V+x_0)$ denotes the closed $\delta$-neighborhood of a suitable translate of $V$. Note that the exponent is optimal because of scale invariance. In particular, when $\mathcal D(\mu)=0$, the support of $\mu$ is included in an $m$-dimensional affine plane. We use this fact to give a simpler proof of Preiss's rectifiability theorem: while still based on Gaussian averages of $\mu$, this new proof avoids showing uniqueness (and hence conicality) of blow-downs of $m$-uniform measures, as well as studying Gaussian-weighted moments beyond second order. The strategy of proof consists of an anisotropic blow-down of $\mu$, followed by an analysis of the resulting Young measure, using a rigidity lemma involving the heat semigroup.

papers.title: Drift and joint minimal displacement for groups acting on hyperbolic spaces
papers.abstract: We obtain a uniform lower bound for the drift of random walks on hyperbolic spaces in terms of joint minimal displacement. Our main theorem applies to weakly acylindrical actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and is quantitative in all relevant constants. For discrete isometry groups of Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature, the required assumptions are automatically satisfied by the Margulis lemma. This yields uniform gaps at zero in drift spectra for pinched negatively curved Hadamard manifolds, hyperbolic groups, and mapping class groups acting on curve graphs.

papers.title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
papers.abstract: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties.

papers.title: LU-type factorizations and Darboux transformations for continuous-time birth--death processes
papers.abstract: We study LU-type factorizations of the infinitesimal generator of a possibly nonconservative birth--death process on $\mathbb{N}_0$, and characterize those for which the corresponding Darboux transformations, obtained by reversing the order of the factors, are again infinitesimal generators of birth--death processes. Two types of factorizations are considered: lower--upper (LU) and upper--lower (UL). In the LU case, the factorization is uniquely determined once the absorption rate of the Darboux-transformed process is fixed, whereas the UL factorization involves an additional free parameter. For both cases we obtain closed-form expressions for the coefficients of the factors in terms of the birth--death rates, determine the exact ranges of the parameters for which the Darboux transforms are birth--death generators, and give probabilistic interpretations of the coefficients in terms of hitting probabilities, expected passage times and occupation times. We also describe the associated spectral transformations (Christoffel and Geronimus transforms) and orthogonal polynomials, and study when the Darboux-transformed process again has a uniquely determined spectral measure: this is always the case for the UL factorization, while for the LU factorization it is characterized by the divergence of a single explicit series. The general results are illustrated with the $M/M/1$ queue, for which all the quantities involved can be computed explicitly.

papers.title: Universality of the conformal anomaly
papers.abstract: The sewing operation is the fundamental algebraic structure of the (infinite-dimensional) Segal moduli spaces as the conformal cobordism category. We prove a universal property of local $\mathbb{R}_+$-extensions of the sewing operation, characterizing them by one real parameter: their central charge. Our result is an analogue of ``Mumford's theorem,'' that appeared in Segal's monograph [Seg88, Seg04], classifying complex extensions, also known as one-dimensional modular functors. Algebraically, the real extensions are characterized by real-valued cocycles on pairs of surfaces under sewing. We identify the disk-disk cocycle as the universal Liouville action, also known as loop Loewner energy. The real determinant line bundle encodes the trace anomaly of euclidean two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFT) and the restriction function of Schramm-Loewner evolution (SLE) loop measures. It serves as the guiding example in our setup and proof strategy, providing the universal $\mathbb{R}_+$-extension. Our results thus give a mathematical explanation for the appearance of the central charge in CFT and SLE, and prove the conjectured uniqueness of Brownian loop measures as the canonical restriction function for SLE.

papers.title: Harmonic Reduction of Spin-Coupled Grover Walks on Hypercubes via Quantum Bernoulli Noises
papers.abstract: We consider spin-coupled Grover walks on hypercubes within the framework of quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN). We identify parity-dependent harmonic subspaces generated by the central Hamming layers: in even dimension they give a fixed-point subspace, whereas in odd dimension the walk reduces on the harmonic subspace to an explicit eight-dimensional reduced dynamics. Using symmetric-group representation theory, we characterize the corresponding isotypic structure and determine the reduced spectrum. The harmonic reduction also yields explicit long-time probability behavior and shows that the resulting states may occupy an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the hypercube while still spanning its full Hamming diameter.

papers.title: Two-Species Boltzmann--Kac Kinetics with Matsumoto--Yor Nonlinear Collisions: Conserved Energy and Conic Equilibria
papers.abstract: We extend Mark Kac's kinetic framework from single-species Euclidean spaces to a two-species, non-linear interaction space on the open cone $(0, \infty)^2$ governed by the Matsumoto--Yor rational collision involution. We identify a non-linear conserved energy $E(x,y) = x + y + 1/x$ and an invariant conic metric measure $d\mu = \frac{dx \, dy}{x(x+y)}$. By establishing a two-species $H$-theorem, we prove that entropy production vanishes if and only if post-collision velocities are statistically independent ($I(U;V)=0$). In contrast to the transform-domain proof of Letac and Weso{\l}owski~\cite{letac2000}, which relies on joint Laplace transforms of general measures, our approach yields a direct physical derivation in state space via the transformation law for logarithmic gradients and separation of variables. This uncouples the functional-differential system to uniquely characterize the Generalized Inverse Gaussian (GIG) and Gamma distributions as the non-equilibrium thermodynamic equilibria.

papers.title: Percolative MDLA: phase transition and critical behaviour
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce the model of Percolative MDLA (PMDLA) on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ which engulfs the entire occupied percolation component of each particle that reaches the aggregate. We prove a phase transition of finite time explosion, as a function of the particle density $\lambda$, where the critical value equals $\lambda_c=-\log(1-p_c^{\rm site}(\mathbb{Z}^2))$. Below $\lambda_c$, the process is nonexplosive and has a linear upper bound on its radius. For $2/3<\lambda<\lambda_c$, it also has a linear lower bound on the growth rate. Above $\lambda_c$, an infinite component is swallowed in finite time a.s. At $\lambda_c$, every update is finite, but the updates accumulate in finite time, causing a blowup. Excluding criticality, the results are generalized to all higher dimensions.

papers.title: Exponential functionals of two random walks and stationary measures of discrete growth processes
papers.abstract: We study random walks with geometric or log-gamma increments, reweighted by certain exponential functionals. We establish precise asymptotics for all moments of exponential functionals, revealing a phase transition as the drifts of the walks vary. To describe the large time limit of reweighted random walks, we introduce a discrete $T$ transformation on random walk paths and establish Girsanov relations. As a corollary, we show that the stationary measures of geometric last passage percolation and the log-gamma polymer on a strip converge to their half-space counterparts as the strip width tends to infinity. In the log-gamma case, this provides an alternative proof of a recent result in arXiv:2607.17030.

papers.title: Supercritical sharpness for Ising double random currents
papers.abstract: We show that the percolation model induced by the double random current representation of the Ising model on $\mathbb Z^d$, with $d\geq 3$, satisfies local uniqueness of the macroscopic cluster with high probability for every $\beta>\beta_c$, uniformly in boundary conditions (i.e. sources). Such a result is sometimes called supercritical sharpness in percolation theory and yields a detailed description of the model via standard renormalisation techniques. As applications, we show the exponential decay of truncated correlations for the Ising model and exponential mixing for the FK-Ising measure, results previously obtained by Duminil-Copin, Goswami and Raoufi. However, our proof is considerably simpler, as it replaces the use of a highly technical multi-valued map principle with a simple sprinkling argument.

papers.title: Anomalous scaling law for the two-dimensional Gaussian free field
papers.abstract: We consider level-set percolation for the Gaussian free field $\varphi$ on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ regularised by a mass of order $N^{-2}$, and investigate the probability $\theta_N(a)$ that the cluster of the origin in $\{\varphi \geq \sqrt{g_N} a\}$ reaches distance $N$ while remaining finite, where $g_N$ is the variance of $\varphi_0$. We prove a scaling law for $\theta_N(a)$ which is quantitative simultaneously in $a$ and $N$. It asserts that $\theta_N(a)=\theta_{\xi}(a_*)(N/\xi)^{-\vartheta+o(1)}$ as $N/\xi\to\infty$, where the correlation length $\xi$ diverges exponentially as $a$ approaches the critical level $a_*$, the critical one-arm probability $\theta_{\xi}(a_*)$ decays fractional-logarithmically, and the exponent $\vartheta$ is explicit and given by a variational problem involving the logarithmic energy. Thus $\theta_N(a)$ crosses over from fractional logarithmic decay at and near criticality ($N\lesssim\xi$) to polynomial decay away from it ($N\gg\xi$), in stark contrast with dimension three and higher, where similar observables exhibit polynomial decay at and near criticality and rapid decay away from it. The proof relies on a coarse-graining scheme capturing a polynomial rate with sharp exponent, and on sharp logarithmic capacity estimates for planar "porous" sets.

papers.title: Angles and volumes of simplices, boxes, and crosspolytopes in constant curvature
papers.abstract: We determine, up to isometry, the Riemannian tangent and normal cones at arbitrary faces of boxes, acute orthocentric simplices, rectangular simplices, and asymmetric crosspolytopes in spaces of constant sectional curvature $\kappa\in\mathbb R$. Using these descriptions, we derive explicit one-dimensional integral formulas for their internal and external angles in arbitrary dimension. In particular, our results cover regular simplices, cubes, and crosspolytopes, the three families of regular polytopes existing in every dimension. We also establish a correspondence between regular simplices and cubes with isometric local cones at corresponding faces, provided their edge-length parameters are suitably matched. Combining our angle formulas with the Poincar\'e relation, we obtain volume formulas for simplices and crosspolytopes in even dimensions. For boxes, we derive volume formulas valid in every dimension. Among the new results are angle formulas for spherical and hyperbolic cubes and crosspolytopes, volume formulas for asymmetric crosspolytopes, and a one-dimensional integral representation for the internal angles of regular crosspolytopes that appears to be new even in the Euclidean case. The formulas involve the standard normal distribution function $\Phi(x)$ and its values at purely imaginary arguments $\Phi(\mathrm{i} x)$. For example, if $d\geq 2$ is even, then the volume of the ideal regular simplex in the $d$-dimensional hyperbolic space of curvature $\kappa=-1$ is given by the absolutely convergent integral $$ \frac{\pi^{d/2}} {\sqrt{2}\,\mathrm{i}^{d}\, \Gamma\left(\frac{d+1}{2}\right)} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \left[ \Phi\left(\frac{\mathrm{i} y}{\sqrt d}\right)^{d+1} + \Phi\left(-\frac{\mathrm{i} y}{\sqrt d}\right)^{d+1} \right] \mathrm{e}^{-y^2/2}\,\mathrm{d}y. $$

papers.title: Delta functions, a local coarea formula and marginal distributions
papers.abstract: We define multidimensional delta functions as generalized functions by pulling back the Dirac delta function, as well as products of such. We prove various formulas including a local version of the coarea formula and we use delta functions to compute marginal probability distributions on spheres.

papers.title: On rigidity of infinite exchangeable sequences
papers.abstract: We ask when the law of an infinite exchangeable sequence is uniquely determined by a finite-dimensional marginal. For mixtures of a probability kernel, a weak localization condition makes three coordinates determine the directing law. Completeness alone makes four coordinates sufficient. Neither order can be lowered in general. For exponential kernels with a nonnegative sufficient statistic, a M\"untz-Sz\'asz support condition implies three coordinates suffice. In the scalar case, this result is sharp. We also characterize when completeness holds simultaneously for all scalar mixing laws by a weighted M\"untz density condition and show that statistic support alone need not decide completeness. These methods yield sharp finite-dimensional refinements of Freedman's theorem on rotatable sequences, namely that spherical symmetry of three coordinates makes an infinite exchangeable sequence rotatable while symmetry of the first two coordinates is in general insufficient. Finally, for energy-radial densities we give a complete-monotonicity criterion for infinite extendibility and determine the exact uniqueness thresholds for $\ell_q$-norm exponential laws.

papers.title: Moment-optimal Gamma approximation of Bessel Process exit times
papers.abstract: We construct finite Gamma convolutions approximating the first hitting time of $1$ by a Bessel process of index $\nu>-1$ started at the origin. The scale measure in the classical exponential representation of this law is obtained by squaring the positive half of a dilated modified Lommel polynomial orthogonality measure. Its Jacobi recurrence yields an $N$-factor Gamma convolution that uniquely matches the first $2N$ cumulants, the maximal number attainable in this class. From an exact Gaussian quadrature remainder we derive supergeometric convergence of the Laplace transforms on compact subsets of a common slit plane and geometric convergence of the distribution functions uniformly on the real line. The approximants have total Gamma shape $N(N+\nu+1)$, and their Laplace transforms and negative moments decrease to those of the exit law.

papers.title: Heat Kernel Estimates for Random Walks with Killing on Transient Graphs
papers.abstract: We give matching two-sided estimates for heat kernels obtained from Schr\"odinger operators $\Delta+W$ on weighted graphs. The graphs we consider are transient and admit two-sided sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates for the Laplacian $\Delta$, and the potentials $W$ decay to zero at infinity. We offer two proofs for one of our main results: one using the Feynman-Kac formula, and one without using it. Our results apply to fractal-type graphs such as graphical Sierpinski carpets, among other examples.
